Consider the ellipse centered at ${CENTER}$ with horizontal radius ${A}$ and vertical radius ${B},$ as shown above. Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$  traverse the ellipse once in the counterclockwise direction starting at the point $A{START}?$
solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the point $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +h,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +k,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Under this parametrization, the ellipse is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, starting from $(h+a,k).$

In our case, the ellipse is centered at the point ${CENTER},$ $a={A}$ and $b={B}.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the ellipse are 

$$
{FINAL},\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
